verdict: WEC Energy earned $389M, up 43%, as warmer weather, new Wisconsin rates and very large new customers lifted electricity sales — and it raised its 2026 guidance.

kpis.label: 2026 EPS guidance
kpis.note: raised and narrowed with this report

segments.name: Wisconsin utilities
segments.note: Electric and gas utilities in Wisconsin (We Energies, Wisconsin Public Service and others) selling to outside customers — the heart of the company. The segment contributed $362M of net income.

segments.name: Illinois gas utilities
segments.note: Peoples Gas and North Shore Gas in Chicago and its suburbs — a seasonally quiet quarter for heating gas; revenue was flat.

segments.name: Non-utility energy infrastructure
segments.note: We Power's generating plants, gas storage and majority-owned renewable projects — sales to outside customers only (it also sold $119M to WEC's own utilities, eliminated here).

segments.name: Other states gas utilities
segments.note: Gas utilities in Minnesota and Michigan (Minnesota Energy Resources, Michigan Gas Utilities).

opex.name: Other operation & maintenance
opex.note: Running and repairing power plants, wires and gas networks, and serving customers day to day.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of plants and networks over their long lives — rises as WEC builds.

opex.name: Property & revenue taxes
opex.note: Property taxes on plants and networks, plus revenue-based taxes.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $242M, partly offset by $50M of other income (including allowance for funds used during construction); the line also absorbs about $1M of subsidiary preferred dividends and amounts attributable to noncontrolling interests, so the flow lands on the $389M attributable to common shareholders. Separately, WEC's roughly 60% share of the American Transmission Company added $66M of equity earnings (the equityM line).
footerNote: Adaptation for a utility: fuel and purchased power ($559M) plus the cost of natural gas sold ($92M) are treated as cost of revenue — together they are WEC's reported cost of sales. Segment revenues are external revenues from the Form 10-Q segment note; the electric transmission segment earns through equity earnings, not revenue. WEC reports in tenths of millions; whole millions are rounded.

takeaways.title: Wisconsin carried the quarter
takeaways.text: The Wisconsin segment contributed $362M of net income, up 29%, on new rates in effect since January, warmer summer weather and carrying costs on construction for very large customers (VLCs) — the data-center-style loads arriving in Wisconsin.

takeaways.title: People used more power
takeaways.text: Retail electricity deliveries rose 3.3% excluding the iron-ore mine and the very large customers — residential use rose 5.1% in the warm weather.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised
takeaways.text: WEC raised and narrowed its 2026 EPS guidance to $5.60–$5.64, citing favorable weather and capital investment supported by the very large customers.
